{
  "thinking": "The sketch has a 90-degree turn where the start stem meets the body outline, and the fluke strokes leave the tail at steep angles. Sofia is about to lock, so I'll flag it now and dry-run to confirm.",
  "say": "Sofia, before you lock, one mechanical thing. Where the start stem drops onto the back, the run has to turn sharply to go along the top and round the bottom, and the fall won't make that corner. Easiest fix: start at the nose, so the top and bottom lines both leave going gently forward and meet at the tail. The fluke and spout should also leave their lines at a shallow angle, not straight up. Keep the spout joined to the body, and no eye. Jack and I will split the strokes once you lock it.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [8, 6],
  "do": "stop",
  "check": "dry_run",
  "notes": "Whale agreed. Dry run of Sofia's first sketch: stem 5 down into the back node makes a 90-degree corner into strokes 1 and 2, so it fails. Flukes 3 and 4 leave the tail too steeply, and spout 6 is tiny. Suggested: start at the nose, top and bottom lines go to the tail, fluke leaves at a shallow angle. I take stroke 1 once locked; split the rest with Jack."
